AcceptanceGrade.description: Verdict from the post-run acceptance gate.
AcceptanceGrade.title: AcceptanceGrade

AgentAction.description: Terminal action chosen by the mind on a given turn.
AgentAction.title: AgentAction

Artifact.description:
The published output of a Run.  Lives in docs/runs/<run_id>/ in the
spawned repo and (when configured) at a GitHub Pages URL.  Functional
artifacts are the deliverable; plan-document artifacts get caught by
the acceptance gate.

answer_md.description: Contents of answer.md (the agent's narrative of what was built).

built_at.description: When the artifact was committed and published.

files.description: Files in the artifact directory.  Embed inline -- ArtifactFile only exists as part of an Artifact.

id.description: Artifact id (typically composed of question id + run id).

run.description: The Run that produced this artifact.

source_repo_url.description: URL of the spawned per-question repo on github.com.

verified_at.description: When the artifact was last verified by inspection.

Artifact.title: Artifact

ArtifactFile.description: A single file inside an Artifact directory.

sha256.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the file contents.

ArtifactFile.title: ArtifactFile

Asker.description:
A person who interacts with the bbot pipeline.  Identity bridges Slack
(via slack_user_id) and GitHub (via github_handle).  An Asker is durable
across questions -- preferences and history accumulate.

affiliation.description: Group or institution affiliation (e.g. "BBOP at LBL").

email.description: Email when known (sometimes from Slack profile).

first_seen_at.description: When this asker was first observed by the pipeline.

id.description: Internal stable id (we use slack_user_id when known, else github_handle).

Asker.title: Asker

BuildMaturity.description:
Distinguishes a proof-of-concept attempt from a production-handoff
attempt.  A prototype and a finished application are different things,
and the agent's strategy + the acceptance rubric vary accordingly.

The mind sets this at intake based on the asker's words.  When in
doubt, default to `prototype` -- most bbot questions are prototyping
questions.  `production_handoff` is the explicit signal that the
asker is past prototyping and wants a credible path to a real shipped
product, which usually means the deliverable shifts to a static_report
describing that path rather than a freshly-built app.
BuildMaturity.title: BuildMaturity

ConversationTurn.description:
A single turn in a conversation -- Slack message, GitHub issue body, or
GitHub issue comment.  Captures who said what, when, in which surface,
and (for mind turns) what action was chosen.

action.description: Action the mind chose for this turn (mind turns only).

channel_or_issue.description: Slack channel id or GitHub issue number (as a string).

intent.description: Classified intent of the turn (e.g. "intake", "status_query").  Free-text for now.

question.description: The Question this turn relates to, when applicable.

reason.description: Free-text reason for the action (mind turns only -- aids audit).

run.description: The Run this turn relates to, when applicable.

speaker.description: The Asker if speaker_kind=asker.  None otherwise.

speaker_kind.description: What kind of entity authored the turn.

text.description: Visible text of the turn (after mention-stripping etc.).

tool_calls.description: JSON-serialised list of tool calls made on this turn (mind turns only).

ConversationTurn.title: ConversationTurn

DeliverableKind.description:
What the asker wants delivered.  Every kind ASSUMES delivery via GitHub
Pages by default -- the Pages URL is the deliverable's home, even when
the substantive output is a downloadable artifact and Pages serves the
explanation / index page for it.  The Pages site IS the durable group
memory of what was built; bare answer-in-issue is the exception that
requires justification.

The acceptance gate dispatches on this enum.  Mismatch (asker wanted X,
agent delivered Y) is a failure independent of whether the delivered Y
is substantive.
DeliverableKind.title: DeliverableKind

ExecutorKind.description: The agent runtime engine that drove a Run.
ExecutorKind.title: ExecutorKind

Kit.description:
A reusable, human-authored bundle of CLASS-expertise for a run -- domain
context, skill/tool hints, libraries, resources, and optional run hints.
Attached to a request (a kit:<name> on the issue) and merged into that
run's BRIEF.md, so it shapes what the autonomous agent does WITHOUT anyone
editing the agent / CAT / BBOT.  The human surface for customization;
authored as plain YAML (see prototype/kits/README.md), this class is the
contract behind it.  Distinct from the per-run issue/BRIEF: the issue
carries this-run specifics, the kit carries reusable how-to-build-this-class.

applies_to.description: Signals CAT uses to pick this kit as a default for a task.

context.description: Domain background injected into the BRIEF.

description.description: One line -- what this kit is for.

libraries.description: Packages the agent may install / use.

maintainers.description: GitHub handles of who owns / curates the kit.

name.description: Stable kebab-case id; the kit:<name> handle.

run_hints.description: OPTIONAL suggested run config -- the agent MAY override (kits inform; the engine decides how to run).

skills.description: Hints on approaches / tools the agent should use.

Kit.title: Kit

KitApplicability.description: Signals CAT uses to pick a default kit for a task.  Embed inline -- only exists as part of a Kit.

deliverable.description: Which deliverable kinds this kit suits.

topics.description: Free-text topic phrases for CAT's semantic match.

KitApplicability.title: KitApplicability

KitResource.description: A doc / API / data resource a kit points at (set url OR drive).  Embed inline.

drive.description: A Drive file id shared with the reader SA.

note.description: What it is / when to use it.

KitResource.title: KitResource

KitRunHints.description: Optional run-config suggestions a kit offers (the agent may override).  Embed inline.

keep_in_mind.description: Constraints / cautions to carry into the run.

KitRunHints.title: KitRunHints

Profile.description:
bbot Issue Form profile -- captures who is asking and the rough scope.
Profile is orthogonal to DeliverableKind (what kind of output is wanted);
a developer-profile question can legitimately want a plan document, and a
researcher-profile question can legitimately want a working artifact.

Historical note: the enum used to include `group_member` for short
logistical / policy / HOWTO questions.  That whole class is now handled
by the secretarial path (cat answers in Slack + files a closed
`kind:secretarial` bbot issue; no bbot-run spawn).  See QuestionKind.
Historical issues with `profile:group-member` labels remain valid;
the label survives independently of the enum.
Profile.title: Profile

Question.description:
A research or engineering question filed against bbot.  Lives as a
GitHub Issue on bbop-skunkworks/bbot; runs accumulate as the question
progresses.  Predecessors capture V2-of-X relationships explicitly.

additional_askers.description: Other askers credited on this question (e.g. collaborators).

body.description: Issue body markdown (the manifest the agent reads).

build_maturity.description:
Whether the asker wants a prototype (proof-of-concept / feasibility
check) or a production-handoff (path-to-shipped-product analysis).
The acceptance gate's strictness on quality / testing / sanding
varies based on this -- a prototype is judged on does-it-work and
is-it-compelling; a production-handoff is judged on does-it-document
the-path-forward credibly.  Defaults conceptually to `prototype` if
not explicitly set by the asker (most bbot questions are prototypes).

REQUIRED for normal bbot-run issues; OMITTED for secretarial issues.

deliverable_kind.description:
What the asker wants delivered.  The mind sets this at intake based
on the asker's words and prior context.  Default expectation across
ALL kinds (except answer_in_issue) is a GitHub Pages site -- what
varies is whether that page is an interactive app, an interactive
report, a static report, or an index for downloadable artifacts.

The acceptance gate dispatches on this slot to pick the right rubric.
Getting it wrong is the #1 way the pipeline mis-grades: bbop#38 was
filed with the implicit assumption of interactive_app but the agent
delivered a static_report, and the gate (correctly) rejected it as
wrong_kind.

REQUIRED for normal bbot-run issues; OMITTED for secretarial issues.

filed_by.description: Which entity actually filed it (a human, the mind, etc.).

final_artifact.description: The most recent or authoritative artifact for the question.

issue_url.description: HTTPS URL of the GitHub issue.

kind.description:
Categorical shape of the issue.  Distinct from `profile` (which
classifies bbot-run *work*).  Absent for normal bbot-run issues.
Explicit kinds opt into different flows -- today only
`secretarial` exists (cat answers + records, no spawn).

kits.description:
Kits applied to this question -- the `kit:<name>` labels resolved to
their definitions.  Provenance of which reusable class-expertise
bundles were merged into this run's BRIEF.  References Kit by name;
the kit definitions live in the public bbop-skunkworks/kits repo.

labels.description: GitHub labels currently on the issue.

predecessors.description: Prior questions this one builds on (V2-of-X relationship).  References by id; the full Question records live elsewhere.

primary_asker.description: The asker who filed the question.

profile.description:
Issue Form profile -- shapes the agent's brief.  Captures asker
context, NOT what kind of output is expected (see deliverable_kind).
REQUIRED for normal bbot-run issues; OMITTED for secretarial
(kind=secretarial) issues which do not run.

runs.description: Run records for this question, newest first.  Runs are intrinsic to the Question they're for; embed inline.

slack_thread_permalink.description: Permalink to the Slack thread this came from (when applicable).

Question.title: Question

QuestionKind.description:
Categorical shape of a Question issue.  Distinct from `profile`
(which classifies bbot-run *work*) -- `kind` classifies whether a
bbot run happens at all.  The label `kind:<value>` is applied to
the GitHub issue at filing time.

Absence of a kind label implies a default bbot-run-bound issue
(its profile + ready label drive the spawn workflow).  Explicit
kinds opt into different non-run-bound flows.
QuestionKind.title: QuestionKind

QuestionStatus.description: Phase of a bbot question's lifecycle.
QuestionStatus.title: QuestionStatus

Run.description:
A single execution of the agent against a Question.  Records what
happened, what was produced, and the acceptance gate verdict.  Multiple
runs per Question are possible (re-runs after needs_iteration).

acceptance_reason.description: Free-text rationale from the acceptance gate.

artifact.description: Artifact produced by this run.  Embedded inline; the artifact's identity is tied to the run.

attempts.description: How many engine attempts were used (for orient-quit retry).

executor.description: Which agent engine drove this run.

question.description: The Question this run is for.

spawned_repo_url.description: HTTPS URL of the spawned per-question repo.

success.description: Did the engine report success (orthogonal to acceptance grade).

tool_calls.description: Number of tool calls the agent made during the run.

Run.title: Run

Runtime.description: Where and how long an agent run is expected to take.
Runtime.title: Runtime

SpeakerKind.description: What kind of entity authored a conversation turn or action.
SpeakerKind.title: SpeakerKind

VerificationGrade.description:
Human or agent's verdict after actually inspecting the published artifact.
Always interpreted RELATIVE to the requesting Question's deliverable_kind --
a plan_document delivered against a `plan_document` request is `meets_intent`,
whereas the same plan_document delivered against a `working_artifact` request
is `wrong_kind`.
VerificationGrade.title: VerificationGrade
